summary: Recent M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology. Architected a microscopic surface inspection pipeline using image stitching, wavelet denoising, and depth estimation for automated defect characterization, and optimized deep learning inference in Linux with hand-written CUDA C++ kernels and TensorRT, cutting convolution latency ~35% and reaching a 5.2x end-to-end speedup on edge hardware.

experience.title: Research Intern (Capstone)
bullets: Architected a metal surface inspection pipeline for microscopic crack analysis using custom image stitching, wavelet denoising, and depth estimation for automated defect characterization.
Designed a custom wavelet bank (alpha-blended sym6+bior3.5) to suppress low-frequency noise, raising reconstruction quality to PSNR 86 from a PSNR 65 stitching baseline.
Deployed ZoeDepth monocular depth estimation for crack-depth profiling with +/-8% error on 3D surface reconstruction.

experience.title: Research Fellowship
bullets: Trained U-Net segmentation with VGG-16, VGG-19, and ResNet-50 backbones on the BraTS 2020 imaging dataset, evaluated on Dice Score and IoU; engineered the data pipeline for large-scale 3D volumetric inputs.

experience.title: AI/ML Intern
bullets: Fine-tuned DONUT, an OCR-free document understanding transformer, in PyTorch with the HuggingFace VisionEncoderDecoder API, improving validation accuracy from 55% to 93%.

experience.title: Deep Learning Intern
bullets: Trained YOLOv8n object detection on 1,133 annotated images to 83% mAP@50 on held-out validation; exported to ONNX and TFLite for on-device deployment.

projects.name: CUDA Kernel Optimization for VGG16 Inference
bullets: Cut inference latency to 49.2 ms from 73.3 ms (uncoalesced GPU) and 77.5 ms (CPU TorchScript), a ~35% speedup at identical accuracy with 1.5-2x faster convolutions.
Replaced TorchScript convolution layers with hand-written CUDA C++ kernels using memory coalescing, constant memory for weights, and preallocated global buffers.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) - M.S. Capstone, RIT
bullets: Optimized YOLO inference with TensorRT for a 5.2x speedup (56.7 to 10.9 ms, 17.6 to 92 FPS) over eager PyTorch, enabling real-time visual servoing on NVIDIA Jetson.
Built a three-layer distributed pipeline over a unified WebSocket fabric; resolved 11 integration failures to reach 100% pick reliability across 10 trials.

awards: 1st Prize, Poster Presentation - 2D and 3D Image Mosaicing of Microscopic Images, F.C.R.I.T. (2024)
